source: NIST Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program (CAVP) GCM Known Answer Test vectors, under the SP 800-38D GCM specification
section: gcmtestvectors.zip files gcmEncryptExtIV256.rsp and gcmDecrypt256.rsp, '[Keylen = 256]' sections
revision: CAVS 14.0, generated 2012-08-31 (gcmEncryptExtIV256.rsp: 'Generated on Fri Aug 31 11:26:26 2012'; gcmDecrypt256.rsp: 'Generated on Fri Aug 31 11:31:25 2012'). Fetched verbatim from https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Algorithm-Validation-Program/documents/mac/gcmtestvectors.zip on 2026-07-02.

notes: Verbatim import (Stage 73) of a small, named subset of the much larger official .rsp Known Answer Test files (each file contains many hundreds of cases across all Keylen/IVlen/PTlen/AADlen/Taglen combinations) — only the specific '[Keylen = 256] [IVlen = 96] ... [Taglen = 128]' cases below were selected and copied byte-for-byte, each recorded with its exact source file + 1-indexed 'Count' value for traceability back to the full .rsp file. No value was altered; 'Key =' / 'IV =' / etc. field-name prefixes and NIST's line format were stripped as minimal, non-value formatting. This selection distinguishes the standard 96-bit-IV case (all vectors below use IVlen=96) from non-standard IV lengths, which exist in the source files (e.g. IVlen=8, IVlen=1024) but are NOT imported in this stage. gcmDecrypt256.rsp's 'FAIL' marker (in place of a 'PT =' line) is NIST's own official negative/tamper case — an authentication-tag mismatch that MUST cause decryption to fail closed — and is imported verbatim as such, not generated locally. No Rust code reads this file yet.

vectors.description: Encrypt direction, [Keylen=256] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=0] [AADlen=0] [Taglen=128] — empty plaintext, empty AAD.
Encrypt direction, [Keylen=256] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=128] [AADlen=128] [Taglen=128] — 16-byte plaintext, 16-byte AAD (the standard 96-bit-IV case).
Decrypt direction, [Keylen=256] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=0] [AADlen=0] [Taglen=128] — empty ciphertext/AAD, valid tag, decryption succeeds.
Decrypt direction, [Keylen=256] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=128] [AADlen=128] [Taglen=128] — valid tag, decryption succeeds (the standard 96-bit-IV case).

Decrypt direction, [Keylen=256] [IVlen=96] [PTlen=128] [AADlen=128] [Taglen=128] — NIST's own official negative case: the tag does not authenticate this (key, IV, AAD, ciphertext); the source .rsp file records 'FAIL' in place of a 'PT =' line, i.e. no plaintext is defined and decryption MUST be rejected.
